record.paper_title: Some open questions in axion theory
record.original_question: In axion models with electromagnetic duality invariance, equivalently SL(2, Z) invariance, what is the correct relation between the non-perturbative constraints imposed by the duality symmetry on the joint axion-saxion scalar potential and the perturbative loop calculations that seem to generate saxion and axion potentials?

evidence.quote: The SL(2, Z) symmetry strongly constrains the form of the scalar potential for both axion and saxion. It would be interesting to clarify the relation between the non-perturbative constraint from the symmetry and perturbative calculations (e.g., in a theory with electromagnetic duality, one may think that the electron/magnetic monopole loop contributes to the saxion potential in the perturbation calculation, and thus the axion potential as well, with a result that does not appear to respect the axion shift symmetry).

artifact.category_tag: axion-saxion effective potentials and SL(2,Z) duality
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a four-dimensional effective field theory containing a complex scalar modulus τ = a + i s, where a is a pseudoscalar "axion" field and s > 0 is its scalar partner (the "saxion"). Assume the theory enjoys an electromagnetic duality symmetry under which τ transforms by the modular group SL(2, Z) acting via τ ↦ (Aτ + B)/(Cτ + D) with A, B, C, D ∈ Z and AD − BC = 1, and under which the U(1) gauge sector is exchanged between an electric description with electrons of charge e and a magnetic description with monopoles of magnetic charge 1/e, where the gauge coupling is identified with τ. Any SL(2, Z)-invariant scalar potential V(τ, τ̄) must be a function on the fundamental domain of SL(2, Z) acting on the upper half plane and, in particular, must respect the discrete axion shift a → a + 1 induced by the T generator.

On the other hand, a naive perturbative loop computation (for instance, summing the one-loop vacuum energy contributions of an electrically charged particle of mass depending on s and, separately, a magnetically charged monopole whose mass depends on 1/s) appears to generate an effective potential for the saxion s, and through holomorphy/supersymmetric or duality-completion arguments a companion potential for the axion a, that does not manifestly preserve the discrete shift symmetry a → a + 1 nor the full SL(2, Z) invariance.

Formulate and establish the precise relation between:
(i) the non-perturbative constraints on V(τ, τ̄) imposed by exact SL(2, Z) invariance (e.g. that V must be expressible in terms of SL(2, Z) modular forms / automorphic functions on the upper half plane), and
(ii) the perturbative loop-generated contributions to the saxion and axion potentials computed in either the electric or magnetic duality frame.

In particular, identify the mechanism (e.g. instanton sums, summation over duality images, Poisson resummation between electric and magnetic loops) by which the apparently shift-symmetry-violating perturbative contributions combine into an SL(2, Z)-invariant potential, and characterize the resulting axion–saxion potential.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open clarification in the theoretical physics literature on axion models with SL(2,Z) duality. No definitive published resolution reconciling perturbative loop-induced axion/saxion potentials with exact SL(2,Z) non-perturbative constraints was located; related work on modular-invariant effective potentials and electric–magnetic duality discusses partial aspects but does not provide a complete settlement.

status_evidence.title: Some open questions in axion theory
status_evidence.snippet: Lists clarifying the relation between SL(2,Z) non-perturbative constraints and perturbative loop calculations as an open issue.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is identified as an open question in the axion-theory literature.
